WARNING is raised when projected 15-minute demand reaches **1,125 kW** (90% of the 1,250 kW contract capacity). [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Demand status tiers]

That 90% line provides 125 kW of headroom before the contract limit, so operators can act before an exceedance—whose excess demand is charged at 2× the contract price up to 10% over, then 3× beyond that. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Key terms] [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-03_tariff_guide.md#EM-03 Tariff Guide > Exceedance charges]

Demand above the contracted capacity is billed as an exceedance: up to 10% above the contract is charged at 2× the applicable period’s contract price; any amount beyond 10% is charged at 3× that price. DemoTronics’ contract capacity is 1,250 kW. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-04_glossary.md#EM-04 Glossary > Billing and demand terms > Exceedance] [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-04_glossary.md#EM-04 Glossary > Billing and demand terms > Contract capacity]

It predicts the change from an anchor because the original level-target tree model missed contract exceedances: tree models cannot extrapolate above values observed in training, and exceedances were rare in that data. The change target lets the model add heat- or start-up-driven increments to the current load; the anchor is the last completed interval for 15-minute–3-hour forecasts, and the same time last week for day-ahead forecasts. On a hot summer weekday, start the heat-wave procedure when the afternoon forecast has P(exceed) ≥20% (WARNING) or ≥50% (ALARM), or when WARNING occurs before 16:00. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Trigger]

Pre-cool before the 16:00–22:00 peak: with the facilities engineer, lower chilled-water setpoint in agreed steps; keep CH-01 lead and stage CH-02 early. Do not manually start a chiller during the peak, because it is held at 30% for 150 minutes. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 2: pre-cool] The earlier 09:00–16:00 half-peak period is NT$5.85/kWh versus NT$9.39/kWh at peak. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Timing against the tariff]

Hold optional burn-in loading and test runs; use the required staggered start order for any unavoidable start. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 3: hold non-essential start-ups] Confirm EV pause readiness and pause EV-01 immediately at WARNING; it can remove up to 28 kW without affecting production. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 4: EV pause readiness]

During the peak, monitor projected demand each interval. If still above the contract, shed in order: pause EV charging; delay the next BI-01/BI-02 burn-in load; raise chilled-water setpoint +1°C; then lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar—stopping as soon as the projection is below contract. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order] Never shed the server room, a molder mid-cycle, or a reflow oven containing boards. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]

Afterward, restore changes gradually after 22:00; once demand is stable below 1,125 kW, restore in reverse order—pressure, setpoint, burn-in loading, then EV charging—and do not restore all loads at once. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 7: after the peak] [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 5: restore] Record the status, trigger projection, actions/times, interval peak, and probable cause in the shift log. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 4: record]

Follow SOP-04: perform the ultrasonic walk-down during a quiet period—ideally at night or on Sunday—then inspect main headers and branches, prioritizing high pneumatic-use areas (especially injection molding); check fittings, quick couplers, hoses, filter/regulator units, drain valves, blow-off nozzles, the air dryer area, and compressor room. Tag and record each leak, isolate/depressurize and repair it, then re-pressurize and recheck. Finally, watch night load for several nights and repeat the walk-down if it does not return to baseline.
